preconditions.description: The number of people n is between 1 and 200 inclusive.
The number of friendships m is between n-1 and 2000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v and b in (0, 1) for u, v, b in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct valid vertices with a direction constraint b of 0 or 1.
The number of provided edges matches m.
The graph formed by the edges is connected.

postconditions.description: The first line of output is either YES or NO (case-insensitive).

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0].strip().upper() == 'NO' if not exists_valid_assignment(n, edges) else output_lines[0].strip().upper() == 'YES'
postconditions.description: Output is NO if and only if no valid income assignment exists that satisfies all envy constraints.
If the answer is YES, exactly three lines are printed.
The second line contains the maximum possible income inequality (max income minus min income) for the assigned incomes.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0].strip().upper() == 'YES' implies all(0 <= x <= 10**6 for x in a)
postconditions.description: All assigned incomes are non-negative and do not exceed 10^6.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0].strip().upper() == 'YES' implies all(abs(a[u-1] - a[v-1]) == 1 for u, v, b in edges)
postconditions.description: For every friendship, the income difference between the two friends is exactly 1.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0].strip().upper() == 'YES' implies all(a[u-1] + 1 == a[v-1] for u, v, b in edges if b == 1)
postconditions.description: For every friendship with b=1, the income of u is exactly 1 less than the income of v (u is envious of v).
The reported inequality is the maximum possible value among all valid assignments.
